challenges.name: loose-comparison-strict-types-quiz
challenges.title: Predict it: loose comparisons and strict_types
challenges.description: Work out what PHP's == and the loose array functions decide, then pick what declare(strict_types=1) does and does not change.

questions.explanation: array_search and in_array compare with == unless the third argument is true. '73311' == '073311' is true because both are numeric strings and are compared as the numbers 73311 and 73311, so the loose search stops at the FIRST match: index 0, the scratch card, not index 1. '500100.0' == '500100' is true for the same reason (500100.0 and 500100 are equal numbers), so in_array returns true. The strict search compares with ===, which needs the same type and the same characters: '500100' is exactly the string at index 2. 'int(1) bool(false) int(2)' is what you would get if all three were strict.

questions.question: A file starts with declare(strict_types=1); and defines function applyVoucher(int $total, int $value): int. Which statements are true for code in THIS file? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: strict_types changes how scalar values are passed to typed parameters and returned from typed functions, for calls made from the file that declares it. applyVoucher(350000, '200000') is then a TypeError instead of a silent conversion, and the same holds for PHP's own functions: strlen(500100) throws 'strlen(): Argument #1 ($string) must be of type string, int given'. The one conversion strict mode still allows is int to float, so vat(8) for a float parameter works and receives 8.0. strict_types does not touch operators at all: '500100' == '500100.0' is still true; only === or a strict flag fixes comparisons. And it is the CALLING file's mode that counts: a file without the declaration can still call applyVoucher('350000', '200000') and get the old coercion.

options.text: A function vat(float $rate) can still be called as vat(8)
strlen(500100) throws a TypeError instead of returning 6
Calls to applyVoucher from other files that do not declare strict_types become strict too

challenges.name: fix-voucher-redemption
challenges.title: Fix the voucher check that accepts "500100.0"
challenges.description: Hồ Gươm Books prints numeric voucher codes, and two campaigns run at once: 5-digit newspaper vouchers and 6-digit scratch cards, so 73311 and 073311 are different vouchers. The checkout accepts "500100.0" as voucher 500100, gives one customer another customer's voucher, and tells a third that an unused voucher was already used. Fix findVoucher and isUsed so a voucher is found only by its exact code and each voucher can be redeemed once. The test runner reads the vouchers and the codes customers type, and prints the result of every redemption.

tests.name: An exact code works once
tests.expected:
500100: ok, voucher 500100 -200000 VND
500100: already used
073311: ok, voucher 073311 -50000 VND

tests.name: 500100.0, 5.001e5 and 0500100 are not voucher 500100
tests.expected:
500100.0: unknown voucher
5.001e5: unknown voucher
0500100: unknown voucher
500100: ok, voucher 500100 -200000 VND

tests.name: 73311 and 073311 are two vouchers
tests.expected:
73311: ok, voucher 73311 -30000 VND
073311: ok, voucher 073311 -50000 VND
73311: already used

tests.name: The scratch card is redeemed first, then the newspaper voucher
Signs, exponents and decimals do not match a code
tests.input:
voucher 01000 100000
voucher 1000 20000
redeem +1000
redeem 1e3
redeem 1000.00
redeem 1000
redeem 01000
redeem 1000
tests.expected:
+1000: unknown voucher
1e3: unknown voucher
1000.00: unknown voucher
1000: ok, voucher 1000 -20000 VND
01000: ok, voucher 01000 -100000 VND
1000: already used
